DM1 Hackathon — Findings Summary

Team 9 | ACoP 2026 | Compiled by Inez

2026-10-12

Summary of literature review, exploratory analysis, and a cross-check of three independent teammate screens (inez, wangui, natiriva), compiled before per-arm predictive modeling. This document is a summary of findings already generated elsewhere (inez/eda_by_arm.R, wangui/eda.R / covariate_outcome_screen.csv, natiriva_code/script_acop.R) — it does not introduce new analysis.

1. Task context

The hackathon dataset is a simulated 500-patient DM1 clinical trial with three non-randomly-assigned treatment arms: Mexiletine (n=161), Oligonucleotide (n=170), and Tideglusib (n=169). Each arm has its own continuous efficacy outcome and derived binary responder label, populated only for patients in that arm.

Arm N Continuous outcome Responder rate
Mexiletine 161 myotonia_change_12wk (negative = improvement) 29.2%
Oligonucleotide 170 qmt_change_26wk (positive = improvement) 41.2%
Tideglusib 169 tideglusib_composite (0-20, positive = improvement) 47.9%

The organizers’ data dictionary explicitly states that not every baseline covariate is a genuine driver of treatment response: some are deliberately clinically-plausible decoys with no real signal, in a given arm or any arm. Identifying genuine per-arm drivers while separating them from noise is the hackathon task itself. The required pipeline splits each arm separately (stratified by outcome, fixed seed, locked test set) before any modeling; scoring (30 pts) is split evenly across Clinical, Technical, and Communication criteria, with correct covariate identification weighted above model sophistication.

2. Literature review

A PubMed search was run for general DM1 severity/response predictors and for the three specific drug mechanisms represented by the hackathon’s treatment arms.

General DM1 severity / response predictors

CTG repeat length (progenitor allele) is the most consistently replicated predictor of DM1 severity (Cumming et al., Neurology 2019, OPTIMISTIC cohort), modified by age and, in some analyses, sex. Patients whose repeat expands faster somatically (higher somatic mosaicism) develop symptoms earlier than progenitor length alone predicts — supporting somatic_mosaicism_index as biologically plausible. PR interval / cardiac conduction is an established DM1 marker, with reported sex differences in cardiac involvement independent of CTG length (Alen et al., JACC Adv 2026, n=549). Variant repeat interruptions and peripheral blood proteomic markers have also been associated with clinical outcomes independent of raw repeat length.

Mechanism-specific literature by treatment arm

  • Mexiletine (sodium-channel blocker, treats myotonia symptomatically): acts on muscle excitability, so clinical presentation (myotonia severity) is expected to matter more than disease-burden markers; a 6-month placebo-controlled DM1 trial found myotonia relief did not translate into functional gain (6-minute walk distance unchanged).
  • Oligonucleotide (antisense, targets DMPK mRNA directly): Thornton et al. (Lancet Neurol 2023) phase 1/2a trial; mechanism frees sequestered MBNL proteins and reduces toxic mutant RNA, so both molecular (CTG-repeat-linked) and clinical burden may matter. The hackathon dataset uses QMT (quantitative muscle testing) rather than the field’s more common vHOT endpoint.
  • Tideglusib (GSK3-beta inhibitor): Horrigan et al. (Pediatr Neurol
    1. phase 2 trial in congenital/childhood-onset DM1; GSK3-beta activity in blood correlates with muscle weakness (Jennings et al. 2025) and the pathway is implicated in CNS/cognitive involvement (Timchenko review 2019) — motivating cognitive_function and muscle_strength as mechanistically plausible predictors for this arm specifically. The real-world REACH-CDM trial missed its primary endpoint but showed benefit on secondary functional measures.

Implication: covariates with genuine literature backing as per-arm response predictors are ctg_repeats, somatic_mosaicism_index, myotonia_severity, muscle_strength, cognitive_function, pr_interval, and age/disease_duration/sex as effect modifiers. Covariates such as albumin, bmi, insulin_resistance, smoking_status, cataracts, and family_history are real DM1-associated clinical features but were not found to be mechanistically tied to response to these three drugs — making them plausible candidates for the dictionary’s stated “plausible-looking decoys.”

3. Correlation structure and data quirks (inez EDA)

Baseline covariate distributions (medians and full distributions) are broadly similar across the three arms despite non-random treatment assignment — no gross imbalance was visually or numerically apparent. Within every arm, the same recurring correlation structure appears among the genetic/disease-severity markers: myotonia_severity correlates strongly with ctg_repeats (r approximately 0.84–0.89), and somatic_mosaicism_index correlates with both ctg_repeats (r approximately 0.61–0.71) and myotonia_severity. Separately, muscle_strength correlates strongly and negatively with disease_duration (r approximately −0.75 to −0.80) in all three arms — longer-standing disease tracks with lower baseline strength — but is only weakly related to ctg_repeats itself (r approximately −0.06 to −0.21). age and age_at_onset are near-collinear (r approximately 0.87–0.90), as expected since disease_duration = age - age_at_onset exactly. albumin, bmi, and ck_level are essentially uncorrelated with everything else in all three arms, consistent with being decoys.

This collinearity matters because the hackathon’s suggested covariate-ranking method (permutation importance) will tend to split credit among correlated covariates rather than cleanly identifying “the” driver — a caveat worth stating explicitly in the final presentation.

Notable data artifact: albumin is exactly constant (4.18) across all 161 Mexiletine patients, but varies normally (range approximately 3.1–5.4) in the other two arms. It therefore carries zero predictive variance specifically within the Mexiletine arm — independently confirmed by all three teammates’ analyses.

Figure 1. Baseline covariate distributions are similar across arms, with no systematic imbalance from non-random assignment. Boxplots of nine key covariates (ctg_repeats, muscle_strength, myotonia_severity, somatic_mosaicism_index, cognitive_function, pr_interval, ck_level, age, disease_duration) by treatment arm. Medians and spreads overlap closely across Mexiletine, Oligonucleotide, and Tideglusib for every covariate shown, aside from minor differences (e.g., Mexiletine’s ck_level runs slightly higher and more dispersed). This supports treating the three arms as comparable at baseline despite the “weighted by fit” (non-random) assignment mechanism.

Figure 1. Baseline covariate distributions by treatment arm: no systematic imbalance across Mexiletine, Oligonucleotide, and Tideglusib for ctg_repeats, muscle_strength, myotonia_severity, somatic_mosaicism_index, cognitive_function, pr_interval, ck_level, age, or disease_duration (see inez/figures/01_boxplots_by_arm.png).

Within-arm correlation structure among the 13 numeric baseline covariates is shown below for each arm separately. Two correlation groups recur in all three: (1) myotonia_severity, ctg_repeats, and somatic_mosaicism_index move together, consistent with all three being markers of the same underlying genetic disease severity; and (2) muscle_strength is strongly, negatively tied to disease_duration specifically (not to ctg_repeats), consistent with progressive strength loss over the course of disease. albumin’s zero-variance row in the Mexiletine heatmap is visible as blank/NA cells.

Figure 2. Mexiletine — genetic-severity cluster and the near-trivial age/age_at_onset link dominate the correlation structure. The strongest pairwise correlations are age with age_at_onset (r=0.90, expected since disease_duration = age - age_at_onset), myotonia_severity with ctg_repeats (r=0.87), muscle_strength with disease_duration (r=−0.75), and somatic_mosaicism_index with ctg_repeats (r=0.65). ctg_repeats is also moderately negatively correlated with age and age_at_onset (r≈−0.62 to −0.64, consistent with genetic anticipation: longer repeats, earlier/younger onset). albumin’s row/column is blank because it has zero variance in this arm (constant at 4.18 for all 161 patients).

Figure 2. Covariate correlations — Mexiletine. Strongest pairs: age vs. age_at_onset (r=0.90), myotonia_severity vs. ctg_repeats (r=0.87), muscle_strength vs. disease_duration (r=-0.75), somatic_mosaicism_index vs. ctg_repeats (r=0.65); ctg_repeats vs. age/age_at_onset (r~-0.62 to -0.64). Blank row/column for albumin reflects zero variance in this arm.

Figure 3. Oligonucleotide — same genetic-severity cluster, plus a new insulin_resistance/age link not seen in the other two arms. The pattern mirrors Mexiletine: age with age_at_onset (r=0.87), myotonia_severity with ctg_repeats (r=0.84), muscle_strength with disease_duration (r=−0.79), and somatic_mosaicism_index with ctg_repeats (r=0.61). ctg_repeats is also negatively correlated with age_at_onset (r=−0.60). Notably, insulin_resistance correlates with age here (r=0.55) — this pairing does not appear as a top correlation in the other two arms and may be arm-specific rather than a general feature of the dataset.

Figure 3. Covariate correlations — Oligonucleotide. Strongest pairs: age vs. age_at_onset (r=0.87), myotonia_severity vs. ctg_repeats (r=0.84), muscle_strength vs. disease_duration (r=-0.79), somatic_mosaicism_index vs. ctg_repeats (r=0.61), ctg_repeats vs. age_at_onset (r=-0.60); insulin_resistance vs. age (r=0.55) is distinctively present only in this arm.

Figure 4. Tideglusib — the genetic-severity cluster is strongest here, with somatic_mosaicism_index also directly tying to myotonia_severity. myotonia_severity with ctg_repeats is the single strongest pairwise correlation across all three arms (r=0.89), alongside age with age_at_onset (r=0.87), muscle_strength with disease_duration (r=−0.80), and somatic_mosaicism_index with ctg_repeats (r=0.71). somatic_mosaicism_index is also directly correlated with myotonia_severity (r=0.65) — a pairing not among the strongest in the other two arms — and disease_duration correlates positively with age (r=0.61).

Figure 4. Covariate correlations — Tideglusib. Strongest pairs: myotonia_severity vs. ctg_repeats (r=0.89, the strongest pair of any arm), age vs. age_at_onset (r=0.87), muscle_strength vs. disease_duration (r=-0.80), somatic_mosaicism_index vs. ctg_repeats (r=0.71), somatic_mosaicism_index vs. myotonia_severity (r=0.65), disease_duration vs. age (r=0.61).

4. Comparison of three independent EDA/statistical screens

Three team members ran independent exploratory analyses. The table below summarizes each approach’s scope and outcome definition.

Teammate Covariate structure Continuous covariate test Categorical covariate test Train/test split used
inez Within-arm correlation matrices; boxplots by arm - - n/a
wangui - Spearman rho vs. continuous outcome (unadjusted) Kruskal-Wallis vs. continuous outcome (unadjusted) seed 1234, data/derived/split/ (shared)
natiriva - Spearman rho vs. continuous outcome + Mann-Whitney U vs. responder (both FDR-corrected) Fisher’s exact vs. responder (FDR-corrected) seed 5182, own locked_test_sets/ (separate)

Open issue: wangui and natiriva each created their own arm-stratified train/test split with different seeds, stored in different locations. The rubric requires locking one split per arm before modeling, so this needs to be resolved to a single shared split before any model results are compared on a team scoreboard.

4.1 Side-by-side significance comparison

★ = significant unadjusted (p<0.05); ✦ = still significant after FDR correction (natiriva). Spearman rho shown where available (wangui’s and natiriva’s continuous-outcome tests are numerically identical; natiriva adds FDR correction).

Covariate Mexiletine Oligonucleotide Tideglusib

bmi, ck_level, pr_interval, smoking_status, albumin ns everywhere (albumin also structurally constant) ns everywhere ns everywhere (pr_interval borderline, p=0.06-0.10)

A methodological note: sex, cataracts, and family_history appear significant only when tested against the continuous outcome (wangui’s Kruskal-Wallis), not against the binary responder label (natiriva’s Fisher’s exact test). This outcome-definition sensitivity suggests these are weak, borderline effects that should not be leaned on as confident findings.

disease_duration is an exact linear function of age minus age_at_onset. natiriva’s multivariate linear models correctly drop it to avoid aliasing/VIF issues; the team should standardize on dropping it (or one of the three age-related covariates) consistently across all models.

5. Synthesized candidate covariate list per arm

Where literature, within-arm correlation structure, and both teammates’ independent statistical tests agree:

Arm Candidate real predictors
Mexiletine myotonia_severity (dominant), ctg_repeats, age/age_at_onset, somatic_mosaicism_index, phenotype — collinear with each other, mechanistically consistent with a muscle-excitability drug
Oligonucleotide ctg_repeats, myotonia_severity, somatic_mosaicism_index, muscle_strength (its only significant arm, matches QMT-based mechanism), disease_duration, phenotype
Tideglusib cognitive_function (dominant, matches GSK3-beta/CNS mechanism), ctg_repeats, myotonia_severity, age/age_at_onset, somatic_mosaicism_index; phenotype weaker here than other arms
  • Consistent decoys across all three arms, all three analyses, and the literature: bmi, ck_level, pr_interval, smoking_status, albumin (plus its Mexiletine-specific zero-variance artifact).
  • Uncertain / outcome-definition-sensitive: sex, cataracts, family_history, insulin_resistance.

6. Open items before finalizing per-arm models

  1. Resolve the dual train/test split (wangui’s shared split vs. natiriva’s separate locked split) to a single, agreed, locked split per arm.
  2. Standardize handling of disease_duration (exact linear combination of age and age_at_onset) across all models to avoid aliasing/VIF inflation.
  3. Because of the ctg_repeats / myotonia_severity / muscle_strength / somatic_mosaicism_index correlation cluster, permutation importance will likely split credit; consider reporting results at the cluster level, or using a method (elastic net) that handles correlated predictors explicitly, and discuss this collinearity directly in the presentation.
  4. Review natiriva’s elastic net and multivariate linear model (with VIF diagnostics) results once the split is finalized, to see which covariate from each correlated cluster survives multivariate selection.
